rows.o: No token found, please login again
rows.m: No token found, please login again
rows.t: "Token" is an implementation word; the cause is a sign-in that has ended, and the way out is a reload. "Session" is kept for analytics (§ Terminology). This is the `expired` cause, not the retryable one: `§ Voice and tone › Errors` supersedes the Phase 4 hand-off, which put "No token" under retryable. There is no Retry, because trying again with no sign-in cannot work. What the student sees, from the code: the question leaves the composer when the send starts and stays in the thread (`ChatCore.tsx:1041`); the no-token branch then shows this toast and returns before anything is sent (`ChatCore.tsx:762-768`), so the question is never saved, and the conversation a reload restores is read back from the server (`ChatCore.tsx:253-269`) without it. A reload reaches the sign-in page, because every path that drops the token drops the stored user too (`middleware.ts:27-28`, `:47`, `:66-67`, `:82-83`) and the route guard sends a user-less visit to it (`ProtectedRoute.tsx:51`). No control is added: that would be a flow change. The compare lane draws the same sentence in its bubble (`useChatLane.ts:124-127`).
rows.nosafe: the question leaves the box when the send starts (ChatCore.tsx:1041) and the no-token branch returns before anything is sent or saved (ChatCore.tsx:762-768), so there is no form to keep
rows.fix: Your question isn't saved. Copy it, then reload the page to sign in again.

rows.t: Names what is happening in the student's terms, not the mechanism; "session" is the analytics word (§ Terminology), so the sign-in is what is refreshed. It is the automatic renewal, not an error (`ChatCore.tsx:797`): the app asks for a new sign-in itself and the student does nothing. When the renewal fails the app signs the student out and opens the sign-in page (`ChatCore.tsx:798-806`, `useChatLane.ts:152-160`), where S-05.06 says the sign-in has expired once that page reads this redirect (`§ Voice and tone › Hand-offs`); the chat shows no error row for it.

rows: The renewal worked and the app sends the question again by itself (`ChatCore.tsx:815-824`); the student does nothing.

rows.t: A response with no readable body: the code shows `{statusText}`, the status's reason phrase ("Internal Server Error"), which is not the server's own words. A reason phrase and a status line always take the cause line with the status as a support reference (§ Errors 3); quoting is for a message in the response body (§ Errors 2). `{statusText}` is the old text and is dropped; `{status}` replaces it.

rows.fix: Ask your instructor or an administrator about it.

No "I", no "please", no em dash; says what is safe to assume (some fields may be filled) and what to do. The reason is the one the code has: after 15 consecutive client-tool round trips in one turn (`MAX_ROUND_TRIPS`, `ChatCore.tsx:299`) the app aborts the stream, ends the turn and adds this message (`ChatCore.tsx:654-675`). The cap counts steps and nothing detects repetition, so the sentence says that the task took too many steps, not that Kiwi repeated itself or went in circles, which the product cannot know (C16). An earlier draft said "after repeating the same steps"; the repeated-step caption is a different place (SR-6.52, `AgentStepChain.tsx:145-158`: the same tool called three or more times in a row).

The fallback label of a step Kiwi cannot name (`describe(null)`, `AgentStepChain.tsx:131`): "Working…", with the ellipsis, the word the chain's header already shows while the turn runs (`:209`; C13). The rule for the walk state's words: "Thinking…" was the wait before the first step until companion v2 (SR-6.69, the user's own wording and the one concession, G9), and the status line's wait verb is now (CP.19 to CP.23); once a step is running its label names the step, and a step that has no name says only that Kiwi is working, so it claims no process the product cannot show (`§ Voice and tone › Step labels`). `AgentStepChain.test.tsx:80` asks for the header with `getByText("Working…")`: it passes while every step is named, and would find two elements if a step with no name were drawn beside the header.
